title: Is a free market "free" if it's regulated?
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss whether a free market is truly free, prompted by a TV pundit saying "so long free market" during 2008 bailout coverage. They describe the idealized capitalist free market (Adam Smith, supply and demand, competition), argue the US has never had a truly free market, and trace how recessions act as a self-correcting "forest fire" that clears weak companies. They then cite government intervention as evidence against a free market: the SEC, the Sherman Antitrust Act of 1890, the FTC, the FDA, and minimum wage, arguing the US is better described as a "managed economy." The episode closes with a sponsor-style tease and an off-topic segment about Chuck's gambling linked to restless leg syndrome medication side effects.
topics: Amazon dot com dot com bubble

segments.title: Opening banter and the bailout
segments.summary: Hosts banter about the seven billion dollar bailout and a TV pundit declaring the free market gone. Josh says the US never had a truly free market, and they agree to examine why.

segments.title: Ideal capitalism and Adam Smith
segments.summary: They describe capitalism in theory: supply and demand, falling prices when supply outpaces demand, and competition. Adam Smith's view that higher wages make workers more productive is discussed, along with a personal anecdote about commission-based selling at a Georgia park.

segments.title: Recession as a self-correcting force
segments.summary: Recessions are framed as a natural correction in which poorly managed companies and bad investments fail, likened to a forest fire clearing undergrowth. The dot-com bust is cited, with Amazon.com surviving because consumers valued it.

segments.title: Government intervention as evidence against a free market
segments.summary: The hosts argue the US is not a free market because the government intervenes: buying stakes in companies during recessions, creating the SEC after corporate abuses, and acting against monopolies like railroads, Carnegie Steel and Standard Oil. The Sherman Antitrust Act and the FTC are mentioned, along with the FDA and minimum wage. They conclude the US is better called a managed economy.

segments.title: Wrap-up and tease
segments.summary: Josh suggests listeners search the topic on HowStuffWorks and sets up the off-topic story about Chuck's gambling.

segments.title: Chuck's gambling and restless leg syndrome medication
segments.summary: Chuck says his restless legs medication caused compulsive gambling, leading him to casinos in Cherokee, North Carolina. They mention a related HowStuffWorks article on weird prescription drug side effects.
